MAJOR: `current_sha()` now hashes only committed `base..HEAD`; uncommitted tracked edits and untracked files are invisible, so a dirty candidate can reuse a prior clean PASS SHA. This regresses the old `git diff HEAD` behavior and violates AC1’s candidate binding.

Base is resolved from ambient `origin/develop` with no fetch/freshness/fallback. Shallow CI checkouts, detached PR refs, stale remote refs, or non-develop branches either hard-fail or compute a wrong base, inflating the delta and binding evidence to an incorrect base.

Returning `<base>-<diffhash>` removes `HEAD` from the candidate identifier; different heads with the same base and review-relevant diff now collapse to the same SHA. If this string keys evidence, AC1’s base/head binding and auditability are lost.
MINOR: `control_gate.py` and `control_runner.py` now contain identical copies of `current_sha()`; the fix was duplicated instead of shared, guaranteeing future drift.
The new `test-framework/tests/pipeline/test_control_evidence_sha.py` is outside the approved design `affected_files`/review scope and test matrix, so the traceability evidence is incomplete.

The new test covers only `engineering/evidence/**` exclusion; no test covers data-only commits under `data/backlog/**`/`dashboard/**`/`engineering/trails/**`, missing `origin/develop`, or dirty-worktree behavior required by AC1.
NIT: The docstring says “never HEAD/evidence” while the command explicitly uses `HEAD`; this is misleading for maintainers.
SUMMARY: The delta-SHA direction is reasonable, but the implementation is not enterprise-safe: candidate identity ignores dirty/untracked state, base resolution is ambient and brittle, and `HEAD` is dropped from the returned SHA.
The new test validates only the happy path and is outside the declared test matrix.
Duplicated SHA logic across two gates increases long-term drift risk.
